text:
maria: Heads up — just saw a parity issue: JS package published to npm (1.4.2) but pip package 1.4.2 shows 'invalid signature' for customers. Anyone else seeing this? @deploy-bot what happened with the release job?

deploy-bot: Publish job completed. npm: success, pypi: success. Signer key id: 0xAB12. Checksums uploaded. CI run: https://ci.internal/runs/5567 :rocket: 

kevin: Is this the new signing key rotation we rolled out yesterday?

sam: I can reproduce: `pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.2` errors with `ValueError: Bad signature` on wheel. npm install works for me.

alex: We should hold canaries. Suggest tagging npm dist-tag `canary` and yank/unpublish pypi 1.4.2 until we confirm. Alternatives: republish with old key or rotate key again.

maria: Agree. To be safe, I'd like to yank PyPI and keep npm as-is behind a canary tag. Can someone run the rollback checklist?

kevin: Rollback checklist: - yank pypi artifact - remove release note entry + revert dist-tag if applied - notify support and status page - republish with signed wheel (old key or rotated key fixed). Anyone object?

sam: No objections. I'll yank via the PyPI UI shortly and put a note in release notes. (Last time we handled yanks via the web UI).

alex: If we yank, we should also create a patch 1.4.3 with the old key quickly. @maria can you coordinate keys with infra?

maria: On it. Spinning up a key-rotation revert and contacting infra to re-enable the previous signer. Will update in ~10m :eyes: 

ci-bot: Release notes auto-update removed 1.4.2 entry per request from @sam. MR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/-/merge_requests/123

kevin: Once yanked, let's run quick smoke tests for both py/js. Playbook snippet: 
```
python tests/smoke_py.py --package redwood-sdk==1.4.2 || echo 'fail'
node tests/smoke_js.js 1.4.2
```

sam: Running now — will report back in this thread.

maria: If republish is needed, prefer publishing as 1.4.3 and add a deprecation note for 1.4.2. Update CHANGELOG with cause: signer mismatch during key rotation.

sam: Quick update — smoke: Py fail as expected, JS ok. I've Yanked PyPI 1.4.2 and left a note in the release notes + support ticket.

kevin: Thanks. Next steps: Maria -> coordinate key revert, Alex -> build patched 1.4.3, Sam -> verify 1.4.3 when available. Keep npm canary pinned in the meantime. :thumbsup:
